caption: The drawing depicts a single wooden door set within a decorative arched doorway. The door appears slightly open, revealing a dark interior. The frame around the door consists of alternating light gray and white bricks above the door, with a curved arch outlined in red, and with a zigzag pattern following the curve of the arch. At both ends of the arch, there are ornamental scroll-like shapes. Beneath the arch and above the lower section, there is a band with a blue and white decorative motif, bordered by thin red lines. The lower portion of the wall surrounding the door is colored in a muted pinkish shade with wavy textured lines. The ground in front of the doorway is rendered with reddish-brown rectangular tiles. The overall color palette includes shades of brown, pink, red, blue, white, and gray. In the bottom right corner, there is handwritten text displaying a name and the year "1936." The background is left uncolored, focusing all detail and color on the doorway itself.
title: Wall Painting
cluster: #12 — Spanish Colonial Art of the Southwest
